screenings.title: The Scout
screenings.description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible labor of TV production, unfolding as an alternative symphony of a New York grappling with gentrification and a growing erosion of empathy. screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: WINNER of the 2026 Library of Congress Lavine/Ken Burns Prize for Film August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker NOTE: A William Greaves centennial series plays on our repertory screen October 23 – 29. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film, The Helen Frankenthaler Endowed Fund for Films on Art, and The Roy Lichtenstein Fund 2026 100 MIN. USA NEON

screenings.title: Making Marie Antoinette
screenings.description: Dir. Eleanor Coppola. 2026. 86 mins. U.S. DCP. With Sofia Coppola, Kirsten Dunst, Jason Schwartzman. In 2005, Eleanor Coppola filmed her daughter Sofia directing Marie Antoinette at the Palace of Versailles, the first production ever granted access to the palace. For two decades, eighty hours of footage went unseen. Now, twenty years after the film’s release and in fulfillment of her mother’s wish, that footage becomes a film of its own. Making Marie Antoinette follows the making of this landmark production, the creation of Milena Canonero’s costumes, and what it took for Sofia to direct at 34, all the while being watched by her mother. Making Marie Antoinette will be in theaters October 23 and available exclusively on MUBI globally from November 6. Watch an official clip here. Free with RSVP, courtesy of MUBI. The new 20th Anniversary 4K restoration of Marie Antoinette will be in US theaters and streaming on MUBI in the US on October 23rd. MoMI members can screen it early on Friday, October 16. Please note: this event is at capacity. Limited tickets may become available on standby. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

DJ Perry (of Knight Chills fame) stars as Alex Kerwood, a fireman haunted by a mother and baby he couldn’t save, whose grief drives a wedge straight through his marriage. Naturally, the solution is a hunting trip with his buddy Wayne, deep into some very unlucky woods, where things quickly spiral when they stumble on, and dig up, a grave with a three-horned skull in it.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: One in a Million
screenings.description: Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home?

screenings.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 1-3
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. A moving tribute to the necessity of resistance.” – Boris Bastide, Le Monde

screenings.title: Afterimage
screenings.description: Powidoki Poland, 2016 Directed by Andrzej Wajda Starring Bogusław Linda Approx. 98 mins. 4K restoration. Released the year that he died at 90, Wajda’s AFTERIMAGE is the perfect coda to a career devoted to depicting the struggle between repressive governments and the free individual. Based on the life of avant-garde painter Wladysław Strzeminski, who was a target of post-War Stalinist forces, which banned abstract art in favor of state-sponsored Socialist Realism, AFTERIMAGE is a classically made drama with a commanding performance by long-time Wajda actor Bogusław Linda as the artist. Of his compulsion to make a film about Strzemiński, Wajda said, “It’s good to see what happens when art is supervised, controlled, influenced by authority and censorship.” Presented with support from The Ashes and Diamonds Fund for Eastern European Film, The Helen Frankenthaler Endowed Fund for Films on Art, and The Roy Lichtenstein Fund

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

SPLIT ROCK sucks you in with its gorgeous cinematography and impeccable sound design and keeps you on the edge of your seat as you follow these young scientists move closer and closer to peril.

screenings.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 1-3
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. A moving tribute to the necessity of resistance.” – Boris Bastide, Le Monde

screenings.title: One in a Million
screenings.description: Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home?

screenings.title: October Country
screenings.description: Shot over the course of a year (beginning and ending on Halloween), OCTOBER COUNTRY is a vérité-style documentary that follows members of the Mosher family, a working-class family in upstate New York as they reconcile with the hardships of their daily life that includes unplanned pregnancy, sibling estrangement, poverty, emotional despondency and war trauma. October Country examines and provides insight into the fraught intergenerational cycles that can pervade in blue collar households.

screenings.title: Sweet Rush
screenings.description: Tatarak Poland, 2009 Directed by Andrzej Wajda Starring Krystyna Janda, Paweł Szajda Approx. 85 mins. An aging married woman (Krystyna Janda), who lost two sons during the war, becomes fascinated with a strapping young man she encounters one day. In this self-reflexive meditation on death, and the passion of youth, Janda breaks the film’s fourth wall with a powerful monologue on the death of her real-life husband, Edward Kłosiński (who happened to be the cinematographer of Wajda’s MAN OF MARBLE and MAN OF IRON). Experimental in structure, this moving film is itself beautifully lensed by Paweł Edelman, frequent Wajda collaborator who also shot Polański’s THE PIANIST and THE GHOST WRITER. Presented with support from The Ashes and Diamonds Fund for Eastern European Film

screenings.title: The Fly
screenings.description: A brilliant scientist accidentally fuses his DNA with a common housefly during a teleportation experiment gone wrong, triggering a grotesque physical transformation, while his journalist girlfriend deals with the aftermath. The Fly sees director David Cronenberg take his body horror fascination to it’s most tragic and romantic extremes thanks to the lived-in performances from Jeff Goldblum and Geena Davis, and the Academy-Award winning make-up effects by Chris Walas and Stephan Dupuis.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: WINNER of the 2026 Library of Congress Lavine/Ken Burns Prize for Film August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker NOTE: A William Greaves centennial series plays on our repertory screen October 23 – 29. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film, The Helen Frankenthaler Endowed Fund for Films on Art, and The Roy Lichtenstein Fund 2026 100 MIN. USA NEON

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: One in a Million
screenings.description: Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home?

screenings.title: Wicker
screenings.description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.title: The North
screenings.description: The North depicts the grueling and emotional journey of two friends – Chris, a Dutchman (Bart Harder) and Lluis, a Spaniard (Carles Pulido) - who reunite after a decade to re-hike Scotland’s famed 330-mile West Highland Way and Cape Wrath Trail. Brimming with both joy and reservation, they undertake Scotland’s lush, but unpredictable terrain as their days are filled with majestic mountainous vistas, creekside camping, the symphonic strains of wildlife, pummeling rain and a slew of eccentric fellow travelers each on their own paths of self-discovery.

screenings.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 1-3
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. A moving tribute to the necessity of resistance.” – Boris Bastide, Le Monde

screenings.description: Kronika wypadków miłosnych Poland, 1986 Directed by Andrzej Wajda Starring Paulina Młynarska, Piotr Wawrzyńczak Approx. 114 mins. Two graduating high school students fall in love in 1939, on the eve of World War II, in a lyrical coming-of-age film set in the idyllic region of Vilnia. The boy’s strict, militaristic father and superstitious mother get in the way of their budding love, and the pair are blissfully ignorant of the turmoil in the real world that will soon engulf their way of life. screenings.title: The Scout
screenings.description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible labor of TV production, unfolding as an alternative symphony of a New York grappling with gentrification and a growing erosion of empathy. Presented with support from The Endowed Fund for Emerging Filmmakers 2025 89 MIN. screenings.title: Sweet Rush
screenings.description: Tatarak Poland, 2009 Directed by Andrzej Wajda Starring Krystyna Janda, Paweł Szajda Approx. 85 mins. An aging married woman (Krystyna Janda), who lost two sons during the war, becomes fascinated with a strapping young man she encounters one day. In this self-reflexive meditation on death, and the passion of youth, Janda breaks the film’s fourth wall with a powerful monologue on the death of her real-life husband, Edward Kłosiński (who happened to be the cinematographer of Wajda’s MAN OF MARBLE and MAN OF IRON). Experimental in structure, this moving film is itself beautifully lensed by Paweł Edelman, frequent Wajda collaborator who also shot Polański’s THE PIANIST and THE GHOST WRITER. Presented with support from The Ashes and Diamonds Fund for Eastern European Film

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. A moving tribute to the necessity of resistance.” – Boris Bastide, Le Monde

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: WINNER of the 2026 Library of Congress Lavine/Ken Burns Prize for Film August 1972: A reunion of Harlem Renaissance luminaries is held at Duke Ellington’s St. Nicholas Ave. townhouse. Though many of these figures haven’t seen each other in 50 years, sharp memories, vigorous debates, and unsettled scores soon flow through this stunner of a cocktail party, which features (among others): artists Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Richard Bruce Nugent; composer Eubie Blake; poet Arna Bontemps; photographer James Van Der Zee; and activists Richard B. Moore and Louise Patterson. After organizing and shooting this extraordinary gathering, filmmaker William Greaves (SYMBIOPSYCHOTAXIPLASM: TAKE ONE) was unable to complete the film before his death in 2014. One of the cameramen that day was his son David, who expertly reshaped this never-before-seen, newly-restored footage into “a film for the ages…one of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I’ve ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker NOTE: A William Greaves centennial series plays on our repertory screen October 23 – 29. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film, The Helen Frankenthaler Endowed Fund for Films on Art, and The Roy Lichtenstein Fund 2026 100 MIN. USA NEON

screenings.description: Over a decade after MISS REPRESENTATION exposed the media’s contribution to the underrepresentation of women in leadership, this follow-up dives deep into the cultural backlash against women’s agency and power. With the proliferation of AI and deepfakes, a new era of tech-facilitated violence is exacerbating sexism and misogyny in an attempt to control and silence women and girls. With inspiring young women at its core, MISS REPRESENTATION: RISE UP interweaves their personal journeys with powerful voices in media, culture, leadership, and academia to reimagine a future that finally uplifts women and girls.

screenings.title: Rubberhead
screenings.description: Known for his intense work ethic, perfectionism, and obsession with breaking new ground, Steve Johnson created iconic creatures and effects for some of the most beloved horror and sci-fi movies in cinema history. Rubberhead is a humorous and heartfelt portrait of the life and times of one of Hollywood’s most prolific monster makers, as well as a historical journey through the golden age of special effects makeup. Steve shares endless, outrageous anecdotes about his freewheeling adventures in Hollywood, while also telling the inspirational but tragic story of his meteoric rise and subsequent fall. His drive and ambition led to some of cinema’s most groundbreaking effects and techniques, but also to heartbreaking acts of self-sabotage, divorce, and serious struggles with addiction. Rubberhead is a captivating reflection on the game-changing practical FX glory days and a fascinating, entertaining, and moving story of an FX master whose greatest monster may have been himself.

screenings.title: One in a Million
screenings.description: Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home?

screenings.title: The Red Violin + Live Performance | Instruments of Desire
screenings.description: Following the success of 1993’s Thirty Two Short Films About Glenn Gould, director François Girard and co-writer Don McKellar reunited to tell the story of The Red Violin, tracing the titular instrument’s journey from its creation in 17th-century Italy to an auction in 1990s Montreal–and the various musicians and owners it bewitches along the way. Girard mounts a handsome production with location shooting across five countries, from China to Austria, and Samuel L. Jackson shines as Charles Morritz, a fussy instrument appraiser who falls under the violin’s spell while decoding its secrets. Composer John Corigliano won the Academy Award for Best Original Score, and violinist Joshua Bell performed all of the solos in the film.

screenings.title: Rosalyn Drexler: Who Does She Think She Is?
screenings.image: https://anthologyfilmarchives.org/uploads/Who Does She Think She Is_Still 1 copy.jpg
screenings.description: Rosalyn Drexler (1926-2025) was a category-defying creative force. Over the course of her multidecade career, she worked as a painter (creating some of the first examples of Pop art), a novelist, an Obie-award-winning playwright, a film critic, an occasional nightclub singer, and briefly, a professional wrestler.The documentary WHO DOES SHE THINK SHE IS? (1975) provides a window into Drexler’s extraordinary creative universe. Set against the backdrop of the lost artistic demimonde of 20th-century New York, the film – directed by Patricia Lewis Jaffe and Gaby Rodgers – shows the artist rehearsing her madcap cabaret performances, cooking for her family in her art-strewn Manhattan apartment, and speaking candidly about her art, writing, and life. As Newsweek critic Jack Kroll remarks in the film, “[Drexler’s] essential insight is that people and things are completely insane, and she speaks from inside the whale.”The documentary will be accompanied by never-before-seen home movies shot by Drexler and her husband Sherman in the 1940-50s, as well as a panel discussion. The screening coincides with a major exhibition of her work from the 1960s at Garth Greenan Gallery at 25 Greene Street; for more info about the exhibition visit: https://www.garthgreenan.com/ CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

Two upper-class wives, their husbands away for the day, share a few toasts to their pre-marital dalliances—with the same man, who just may be en route from France to visit. Old rivalries and past scandals bubble to the surface in this intoxicating romp from one of theatre’s comedy masters. Starring Golden Globe-winner Rose Byrne (If I Had Legs I’d Kick You) and Tony Award winner Kelli O’Hara (The King and I), with Tracee Chimo, Mark Consuelos (making his Broadway debut), Christopher Fitzgerald and Aasif Mandvi, this new Roundabout Theatre and Tony Award-winning production of ‘pure escapist fun’ (The New York Times) was filmed live on stage at Broadway’s Todd Haimes Theatre and now comes to the big screen.

screenings.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 4-5
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. It’s a crime melodrama, with most of the attendant clichés accounted for and transcended, especially of the last job before retirement from the underworld. It’s a star vehicle, with Pacino riding high at the crest of a resurgence that began with Harold Becker’s superb 1989 thriller SEA OF LOVE and would continue through the 1990s and into the early aughts. Vignettes interlock in surprising fashion, filling in the contours of Puerto Rican gangster Carlito’s life as he emerges from prison and is hit up by everyone for favors.” – Roger Ebert Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.description: ABOUT THE DOWNTOWN FESTIVAL: The Downtown Festival is a multidisciplinary celebration of independent film, music, art, and culture held across Lower Manhattan each October. Founded and directed by filmmaker Rebekah Sherman-Myntti, the festival brings together artists across disciplines and generations through film premieres, anniversary screenings, live music performances, artist talks, and special one-night-only events. Programming is led by Sherman-Myntti and Associate Director Briana Bursten, with a focus on discovery, experimentation, community, and genuine artist-to-artist exchange. The festival’s film program runs October 9-18 at Roxy Cinema, with additional programming and special events taking place all over downtown.

screenings.title: The Musical Vampire
screenings.description: The two films, THE CHINESE GHOSTBUSTER and EXORCIST MASTER (the latter screened as part of our 2023 Fist Fright Marathon) would mark the last time Lam would appear on the big screen as his Taoist priest character, and curiously, both films provide a more in-depth look at Taoist ritual and practice than most of his previous appearances. CHINESE GHOSTBUSTER is largely a riff on the Taoist folk legend of Zhong Kui, a mythological demon slayer known as the “King of Ghosts”, while EXORCIST MASTER operates on a playful contrast between the religious traditions of its two leads, a Taoist priest played by Lam, and a Christian priest played by Wu. Together the films offer a fittingly spiritual coda to the career of a performer whose likeness inadvertently became synonymous with the Taoism itself.

screenings.title: Making Marie Antoinette
screenings.description: In 2005, Eleanor Coppola filmed her daughter Sofia directing Marie Antoinette at the Palace of Versailles, the first production ever granted access to the palace. For two decades, eighty hours of footage went unseen. Now, twenty years after the film’s release and in fulfillment of her mother’s wish, that footage becomes a film of its own. Making Marie Antoinette follows the making of this landmark production, Milena Canonero’s costume work, and what it took to direct at 34, watched the whole time by her own mother.

screenings.title: First We Bombed New Mexico - the Aftermath
screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. An earlier version of the film won 16 festival awards, including Best Director and Best Documentary at the Paris Cine Film Festival, Best Documentary Feature and Best Directing at the Worldwide Women’s Film Festival, and the Jury Prize for Best Historical Documentary at the San Antonio Film Festival. screenings.title: Society | The Surreal Nightmares of Screaming Mad George
screenings.description: Brian Yuzna’s tangle of class warfare, scatalogy and ugly sex is a stupendously unsubtle eat-the-rich satire. The film’s central metaphor, which suits the 21st century even better than it did the Reagan-Bush 80s, presents the wealthy as literally inhuman gluttons. Since time immemorial, this cupidinous race has parasitically feasted on the inferior homo sapiens during “shuntings,” Burroughsian nightmares of viscera, gobs of lube and denatured flesh. The mutations are the greatest showcase of the unnerving surrealistic makeup designs of Screaming Mad George—which went on to be the primary influence on the make-up designs of films like The Substance and Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil.

screenings.title: Persona: 60th Anniversary Screening (Co-presented with NewFest)
screenings.description: Dir. Ingmar Bergman. 1966. 82 mins. Sweden. DCP. “If looked at through the right queer lens, Bergman’s Persona could be among the most penetrating break-up movies ever made.” With his landmark drama Persona, which celebrates its 60th anniversary this year, Ingmar Bergman reached new heights of visual poetry. Liv Ullmann, in her first of many legendary collaborations with Bergman, plays a stage actor who has inexplicably gone silent. Bibi Andersson is equally mesmerizing as the garrulous young nurse caring for her at a remote island cottage. Isolated together, the women perform a mysterious spiritual and emotional transference in a scene that has come to influence generations of filmmaking. Shot by the great Sven Nykvist, Persona remains a penetrating, dreamlike work of profound psychological depth that has long been discussed as a breakthrough tale of unspoken love. The Museum is pleased to co-present this masterpiece on the big screen with NewFest, New York’s Largest Queer Film Fest. Purchase tickets through NewFest’s website. Co-presented with:

screenings.title: Music Video Mischief with director Nigel Dick
screenings.description: 6:30–8:00 p.m. The art and style of rock music videos from the mid 1980s through the early 2000s—the choreography, the fashion, the swooning looks!—defined an era for millennials and GenX. Join us in the Bartos Screening Room to see a selection of ebullient music videos from director Nigel Dick. They include Britney Spears’s iconic “Baby One More Time” and Oasis’s “Wonderwall,” plus videos featuring Cher, Celine Dion, Tears for Fears, Guns N’ Roses, Alice Cooper, Def Leppard, and plenty of surprises, too! These videos show some of the chaos and charm of the era. This free screening will be followed by a conversation with Nigel Dick and Rolling Stone senior writer David Browne about the making of these classics and a book signing of Dick’s Music Video Mischief: Ozzy to Britney, Oasis to Gn’R, McCartney to Cher: a lifetime of rock and chaos (2026, Trouser Press Books), available for sale in the MoMI Shop (store closes at 8:00 p.m.). Free with RSVP. Special Guests: After a brief stint busking in the Paris Metro, Nigel Dick got his start in the music business at London’s upstart Stiff label in the late ’70s. He began a career as a music video director; ultimately working with hundreds of stars, including Oasis, Ozzy Osbourne, Cher, Paul McCartney, Guns n’ Roses, Toto, Britney Spears, Celine Dion, Alice Cooper, Def Leppard, Alice in Chains, and Tears for Fears. If you’ve ever watched MTV, you’ve seen his work. He has directed more than 450 music videos and 35+ documentaries and feature films. He has won three MTV awards, two Billboard Awards, three MVPA awards and one Brit award. His videos have been nominated for a further 21 MTV awards, 26 Much Music Awards, and a Grammy. His book Music Video Mischief is out on Trouser Press Books September 15. David Browne is a Senior Writer at Rolling Stone, where he contributes deep-dive reports, reviews and profiles on music. He is also the author of seven books, including biographies of Sonic Youth, Jeff Buckley, the Grateful Dead, and, most recently Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young: The Wild, Definitive Saga of Rock’s Greatest Supergroup.

screenings.title: Nosferatu + Live Score
screenings.description: Nosferatu + Live Score by the Andrew Alden Ensemble The vampire film that started them all gets its shadow back. The Andrew Alden Ensemble performs an original score live beneath F.W. Murnau’s 1922 landmark — the New York chamber group whose violin, cello, keys, drums, and voice sit somewhere between contemporary classical and rock, writing music built for the room rather than the recording booth: immediate, physical, and made for this film alone. On screen, Count Orlok (Max Schreck) uncoils out of the Carpathians — all talons and teeth and rat-borne plague — and crosses the sea toward a town that cannot wake from him. A hundred years later the images still crawl.

screenings.title: Bram Stoker’s Dracula
screenings.description: Dir. Francis Ford Coppola. 1992, 128 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Gary Oldman, Winona Ryder, Anthony Hopkins, Sadie Frost, Keanu Reeves, Tom Waits. In adapting the original Victorian-era Gothic vampire novel, Coppola pulled out all the stops and then some. For his rendition of the Dracula story, Coppola produced a quirky, idiosyncratic, and over-the-top cascade of lush and violent horror imagery that was, miraculously, a box-office smash. Working with brilliantly self-imposed limitations (all practical effects that would have been possible in the silent era); cramming every frame with monumental sets and matte paintings; and directing Oldman in one of his finest performances as the devilishly romantic Transylvanian count, Coppola created a film so sensational that even the notoriously horror-averse Academy Awards honored it three times, for makeup, sound effects, and Eiko Ishioka’s dazzling costumes. screenings.title: Vampyr + Live Score
screenings.description: Carl Theodor Dreyer’s 1932 fever dream is less a horror film than a nightmare filmed at the moment of waking — fog, drifting shadows, a scythe, a burial seen from inside the coffin. The Andrew Alden Ensemble scores it live with violin, electric guitar, piano, synthesizers, and percussion, the New York group’s music moving with the film’s logic of dread rather than against it. A young traveler, Allan Gray (Julian West), arrives in a riverside village held under the spell of a vampire, and the world begins to come loose at the edges. Dreyer made it as sound cinema was being born and produced something stranger than either silence or speech; performed with a live original score, it turns stranger still.

screenings.title: Freaked | The Surreal Nightmares of Screaming Mad George
screenings.description: One of the quintessential early-’90s cult films, Freaked was adapted by Alex Winter and Tom Stern from their psychotronic MTV series The Idiot Box. Winter plays a vain Hollywood actor who takes a gig promoting an evil South African fertilizer company. But an airplane incident lands him in the middle of a grotesque amusement park, where he is transformed into a member of its expansive freak show. A deliriously grotesque live-action cartoon, Freaked is a carnivalesque melange of eye-popping make-up effects and fun-house set design. It also features an all-star cameo casting ranging from Gibby Haynes of The Butthole Surfers to Mr. T, plus masked appearances from Keanu Reeves and future Wicked director Jon M. Chu. Must be seen to be believed.

screenings.title: The Exorcist
screenings.description: Dir. William Friedkin. 1973, 122 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Ellen Burstyn, Linda Blair, Jason Miller, Max von Sydow. Widely considered one of the scariest films ever made, The Exorcist has shocked and fascinated generations of viewers. Directed by William Friedkin and written by William Peter Blatty, adapting his own best-selling 1971 novel, the film made an essential contribution to the horror genre, pitting the Catholic church against a demon for control of a young girl’s soul. The film’s remarkable, often shocking effects were done by the brilliant and pioneering makeup master Dick Smith (Little Big Man, The Godfather), who transformed the possessed young girl Regan (Linda Blair) into a foul, blasphemous monster. Nominated for ten Academy Awards, including Best Picture, and winning for Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Sound. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. screenings.title: An American Werewolf in London
screenings.description: Dir. John Landis. 1981, 97 mins. U.S. DCP. With David Naughton, Griffin Dunne, Jenny Agutter. The rare humor-tinged horror that manages to be entirely terrifying and quite funny, Landis’s film follows two American backpackers whose destinies are changed forever when they decide to stray from the roads while traveling across rural England. After being bitten by a strange furry animal, David Kessler (Naughton) wakes up in a London hospital and finds himself plagued by ominous dreams and foreboding ghosts telling him to beware the next full moon. Rick Baker’s eye-popping practical makeup effects (which won an Oscar the first year the Academy added a makeup category) enhance this marvelous dark comedy that still has the power to make audiences scream and giggle. Griffin Dunne appears in an unforgettable supporting role as David’s friend, whose death can’t stop him from trying to hang out. screenings.title: Fugs Film!
screenings.description: Formed in late 1964 by Ed Sanders and Tuli Kupferberg, alongside drummer Ken Weaver – anarchic East Village beat poets who could barely play their instruments – The Fugs are credited as the first true underground band. Their lo-fi folk music could be challenging and weird but they had a knack for catchy pop songs, such as “Supergirl” and ‘Slum Goddess”. One of the most crucial figures in countercultural history, Sanders founded the Peace Eye bookstore and the arts journal “F*** You: A Magazine of the Arts”, and, among other late-1960s antics, attempted to levitate the Pentagon and staged a funeral for flower power in San Francisco. Chuck Smith’s vital documentary features eye-popping archival footage and interviews with Sanders, Aline & R. Crumb, Lenny Kaye, Penny Arcade, Jeffrey Lewis, and many others, to tell the story of NYC’s original punks.The screening will be followed by a Q&A with Penny Arcade, Steven Taylor and other participants from the film!CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: The Wolf Man
screenings.description: Dir. Curt Siodmak. 1941, 70 mins. DCP. With Lon Chaney Jr., Claude Rains, Evelyn Ankers, Maria Ouspenskaya, Ralph Bellamy, Patric Knowles, Warren William, Bela Lugosi. Happy homecomings and family reconciliations take a ghastly turn when Larry Talbot is attacked by and kills a wolf during an evening out, though only a man’s body is found after the tragedy. The mystery deepens when Larry learns that this man was a werewolf, and now, when the wolfbane blooms and the autumn moon is bright, he too will make the same transformation. The Wolf Man is the finest horror movie of Universal’s monster revival in the 1940s, celebrated for its spectacular makeup effects by Jack Pierce and Lon Chaney Jr.’s tortured turn in the title role. screenings.title: Fallen Angels by Noël Coward
screenings.description: Sparkling, dizzying, and deliciously potent, Fallen Angels, Noël Coward’s champagne-fresh comedy of bad manners, shocked and delighted audiences at its 1925 premiere. Two upper-class wives, their husbands away for the day, share a few toasts to their pre-marital dalliances—with the same man, who just may be en route from France to visit. Old rivalries and past scandals bubble to the surface in this intoxicating romp from one of theatre’s comedy masters. Starring Golden Globe-winner Rose Byrne (If I Had Legs I’d Kick You) and Tony Award winner Kelli O’Hara (The King and I), with Tracee Chimo, Mark Consuelos (making his Broadway debut), Christopher Fitzgerald and Aasif Mandvi, this new Roundabout Theatre and Tony Award-winning production of ‘pure escapist fun’ (The New York Times) was filmed live on stage at Broadway’s Todd Haimes Theatre and now comes to the big screen.

screenings.title: Baab
screenings.description: Dir. Nayla al Khaja. 2026, 97min. United Arab Emirates. In Arabic, with English subtitles. DCP. With Shaimaa El Fadul, Huda Alghanem, Meera Almidfa. Haunted by the unceasing hum of tinnitus in her left ear and sudden death of her twin sister, Wahida (El Fadul) goes to the remote Ras Al-Khaimah mountains to find solace. Instead, she comes across an eerie green door in her sister’s locked bedroom that seems to blur the line between reality and fantasy, and the living and the dead. In Nayla Al Khaja’s dark fairy tale, an immersive exploration of grief, the audience is plunged into Wahida’s shattered mind, and seemingly ordinary domestic spaces are transformed into an emotional landscape of fear and trauma. Even scarier than the film’s psychological horror-trip is the fact that it has been so hard to see outside of the region in which it was made. Despite al Khaja’s breakthrough talent as the first female Emirati filmmaker, the delighted reviews out of Baab’s premiere at the Cairo International Film Festival, a theatrical run throughout the MENA world, and a collaboration with two-time Oscar award-winning Indian film composer A.R. screenings.title: Magic
screenings.description: Dir. Richard Attenborough. 1978, 107 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Anthony Hopkins, Ann-Margret, Burgess Meredith, Ed Lauter. In this sinister cult classic, a brilliantly unbalanced Anthony Hopkins plays Charles “Corky” Withers, a failed magician turned ventriloquist who begins to show symptoms of psychosis—and allows his dummy, the foul-mouthed “Fats,” to take over his life. Is he shuttling head-first into a mental crackup? Or does the mean-spirited Fats truly have a mind of his own? Genuinely unsettling, this shadowy, emotionally gripping thriller was infamous for its 1970s TV spots, which scarred a generation of unsuspecting kids, but the film is diabolically effective in every way, and features a stellar cast, including a touching Ann-Margret as his love interest. screenings.title: On the Relentless Destruction of Beauty: Short Housing Films + Q&A
screenings.description: On The Relentless Destruction of Beauty features artist studios, communized parks, and residential buildings as spaces produced through—and for—collective creativity, labor, and cohabitation. Spanning the 1960s to the present, the program traces the ways everyday acts of living and making come into conflict with capital’s logic of private property, which seeks to empty such spaces of life in the pursuit of profit. Across these four films, however, the home emerges not as a commodity to be exchanged—nor as an asset to be valued through speculation and dispossession—but as a site of ongoing creative struggle.

Seat at the Table with filmmakers and special guests in person
screenings.description: Followed by a conversation with filmmakers and special guests Dirs. Sarita Khurana and Yoav Attias. 2026, 90 mins. U.S. DCP. Seat at the Table chronicles the rise of South Asian Americans in U.S. politics, tracing a remarkable journey from political disenfranchisement to an increasingly powerful presence in American civic life. Filmed during the 2024 election cycle, Khurana and Attias follow congressional and state-level candidates alongside grassroots organizers, voters, and communities as a record number of South Asian Americans seek elected office. With intimate vérité access, the film captures a community awakening to its political power at a pivotal moment in American democracy. Moving beyond individual campaigns, Seat at the Table explores representation, belonging, and the ways immigrant communities are reshaping who participates in, and ultimately holds power within, American political life. The screening will be followed by a conversation with the filmmakers and special guests about the making of the documentary, South Asian political representation, and the communities helping to redefine who has a seat at the table in American civic life. Free with RSVP.

screenings.title: Azul
screenings.description: AZUL is a documentary about the poetic soul of Nicaragua. Twenty-four poems interweave with interviews to create a narrative of Nicaragua’s poetry and the historical contexts and individuals who formed it. With poems from the creator of Modernismo, Rubén Darío, to Ernesto Cardenal, Carlos Rigby, and Gioconda Belli, to people reciting spontaneously in the street and soldiers workshopping poems on the frontlines, AZUL reveals a nation alive with the creative spirit and a profound belief in poetry as a crucible for change and expression. Originally filmed during the height of the Contra War, the film has been restored digitally.Preceded by:Richard Levine AFTER BASHŌ 2026, 8 min, DCPTwenty haikus by Bob Holman – written while he was following “A Narrow Path Into the Interior,” the walk that Japan’s National Poet, Matsuo Bashō, took in 1689 – are the starting point of this animated collaboration by filmmaker Richard Levine, musician Phillip Johnston, and poet Bob Holman. screenings.description: Paranoid Brigadier General Jack D. Ripper of Burpelson Air Force Base, believing that fluoridation of the American water supply is a Soviet plot to poison the U.S. populace, is able to deploy through a back door mechanism a nuclear attack on the Soviet Union without the knowledge of his superiors, including the Chair of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Buck Turgidson, and President Merkin Muffley. screenings.title: Ganja & Hess | Bill Gunn at Roxy!
screenings.description: Flirting with the conventions of blaxploitation and horror, Bill Gunn’s revolutionary independent film Ganja & Hess is a highly stylized and utterly original treatise on sex, religion, and African American identity. Duane Jones (Night of the Living Dead) stars as anthropologist Hess Green, who is stabbed with an ancient ceremonial dagger by his unstable assistant (director Bill Gunn), bestowing upon him the blessing of immortality… and the curse of an unquenchable thirst for blood. When the assistant’s beautiful and outspoken wife Ganja (Marlene Clark) comes searching for her missing husband, she and Hess form an unexpected partnership. Together, they explore just how much power blood holds.

This is an historic and intimate farewell to Ozzy and the band that changed music forever.

screenings.title: First We Bombed New Mexico - the Aftermath
screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. An earlier version of the film won 16 festival awards, including Best Director and Best Documentary at the Paris Cine Film Festival, Best Documentary Feature and Best Directing at the Worldwide Women’s Film Festival, and the Jury Prize for Best Historical Documentary at the San Antonio Film Festival. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH reveals an unknown story that has captured audiences. The film was a part of the momentum that led to Congress awarding compensation to New Mexico Downwinder families in 2025. The inspirational re-release witnesses a people who were once considered powerless and voiceless finally gaining recognition after years of fighting for justice.

screenings.title: Occupational Hazard: the First Coral Reefers
screenings.description: OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD: THE FIRST CORAL REEFERS is a feature documentary that journeys back to the 1970s and early 1980s to tell the story of Jimmy Buffett’s original Coral Reefer Band. Set against the creative backdrop of Key West, the film explores the musicians, friendships, touring years, and studio sessions that helped shape Buffett’s legendary sound. Through rare, never-before-seen archival footage and deeply personal interviews with founding members, tour managers, producers and music legends, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD captures the camaraderie, chaos, and magic of an era that thrived on freedom and lived without a rulebook. Narrated by Academy-award winner Jeff Bridges, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD offers fans a deeper look at the people behind the music and the era that helped define Jimmy Buffett’s lasting legacy. This film is a tribute to Buffett and the original Coral Reefers, the places and people that shaped them, the volatile beauty of a musical moment that couldn’t last but changed everything and their candid sentiment toward Buffett. It’s the origin story upon which the Parrot Head empire was built upon, by the people who helped lay the foundation.

screenings.title: Halloween
screenings.description: Credited, rightfully, as the film that kickstarted the “slasher” subgenre, Carpenter’s 1978 Halloween is a masterwork of building tension, an exercise in mood and suspense that takes its cues from Hitchcock, unlike most of the 80s gorefests it would inspire. The film’s key innovation – besides the indelibly terrifying image of the blank-faced “shape” aka Michael Myers – is setting it in an innocuous American suburb; there’s nowhere, not even a nice middle class home, where the viewer is safe. Jamie Lee Curtis makes her scream queen debut as one of several babysitters being stalked by a masked, escaped mental patient on Halloween night, her only savior being the patient’s maniacally driven doctor, played with gusto by the great Donald Pleasance. But the secret weapon of Halloween is the score – composed by Carpenter himself – a tinkling, off-meter piano figure that continues to haunt long after the final unsettling frame. A Halloween season perennial.

screenings.title: Prince of Darkness

Met with middling reviews during its original release, Prince of Darkness is now considered one of Carpenter’s greatest achievements in atmospheric terror and features another one of his classic synthesizer scores.

screenings.title: The Vourdalak
screenings.description: Dir. Adrien Beau. 2023, 90 mins. France, DCP. With Kacey Mottet Klein, Ariane Labed, Grégoire Colin, Vassili Schneider. A genuinely eccentric spin on the vampire story, integrating uncanny puppet effects with its live-action storytelling, this unsettling, lovingly crafted—and often funny—period creep-show adapts “The Family of the Vourdalak,” a novella by Aleksey Konstantinovich Tolstoy written in 1839—that’s nearly 60 years before Bram Stoker’s Dracula. Lost in a misty forest on a royal errand, the foppish Marquis d’Urfé, a diplomatic envoy for the King, happens upon a Serbian family’s home for shelter. Their village ransacked by the Turks, the clan nervously awaits the return of its patriarch, who has been gone six days to fight the enemy; upon his return, he has decidedly transformed into something both more and less than human. Adrien Beau’s ingenious twist on vampire folklore has the genuine feel of a classic horror short story, while its daring marionette effects and widescreen, super 16mm cinematography create a singularly eerie experience. screenings.description: Dir. William Friedkin. 1973, 122 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Ellen Burstyn, Linda Blair, Jason Miller, Max von Sydow. Widely considered one of the scariest films ever made, The Exorcist has shocked and fascinated generations of viewers. Directed by William Friedkin and written by William Peter Blatty, adapting his own best-selling 1971 novel, the film made an essential contribution to the horror genre, pitting the Catholic church against a demon for control of a young girl’s soul. The film’s remarkable, often shocking effects were done by the brilliant and pioneering makeup master Dick Smith (Little Big Man, The Godfather), who transformed the possessed young girl Regan (Linda Blair) into a foul, blasphemous monster. screenings.title: Suspiria
screenings.description: Both the pinnacle of his career and the giallo subgenre, Dario Argento’s Suspiria ranks in the pantheon of the greatest horror movies of all time, and with damn good reason. Masterfully employing dream logic (the script was co-written by then wife Daria Nicolodi) and gloriously garish lighting techniques, the film is a true modern fairy tale that tells the story of a ballet student (Jessica Harper) who transfers to a German dance academy only to find it is run by a coven of murderous witches. Argento’s command of shock and suspense is on full display in every blood-soaked scene, but the true secret weapon of Suspiria is the unbelievably scary and propulsive score by the prog rock band Goblin. It all adds up to that rare witches brew: the perfect horror experience.

In French with English subtitles.“This documentary on the slaughterhouses of Paris is one of the great masterpieces of the subversive cinema; here, for once, we are face to face with death, and are neither protected nor cheated. […] A dream-like quality permeates the intense realism of the images; a surrealist intent – akin to Buñuel’s slitting of the eyeball in UN CHIEN ANDALOU – is discernible in this anti-bourgeois film. But the eyeball, however shocking, was fictional; BLOOD OF THE BEASTS is real.” –Amos Vogel, FILM AS A SUBVERSIVE ARTJean GenetUN CHANT D’AMOUR1950, 26 min, 35mm, silent. screenings.title: Halloween
screenings.description: Credited, rightfully, as the film that kickstarted the “slasher” subgenre, Carpenter’s 1978 Halloween is a masterwork of building tension, an exercise in mood and suspense that takes its cues from Hitchcock, unlike most of the 80s gorefests it would inspire. The film’s key innovation – besides the indelibly terrifying image of the blank-faced “shape” aka Michael Myers – is setting it in an innocuous American suburb; there’s nowhere, not even a nice middle class home, where the viewer is safe. Jamie Lee Curtis makes her scream queen debut as one of several babysitters being stalked by a masked, escaped mental patient on Halloween night, her only savior being the patient’s maniacally driven doctor, played with gusto by the great Donald Pleasance. But the secret weapon of Halloween is the score – composed by Carpenter himself – a tinkling, off-meter piano figure that continues to haunt long after the final unsettling frame. A Halloween season perennial.

screenings.title: Ec: Ernie Gehr
screenings.description: “Ernie Gehr [makes] cinematic magic, often from the least likely materials. Indeed, Gehr’s most famous film, SERENE VELOCITY (1970), in which the filmmaker transforms an institutional hallway in the basement of a classroom building at the State University of New York at Binghamton into a nexus of visual and conceptual energy, merely by adjusting his stationary camera’s zoom lens every four frames for twenty-three minutes, can be read as Gehr’s manifesto. For Gehr the most everyday spaces and the most mundane actions offer the imaginative filmmaker the most interesting potential. No other filmmaker, with the exception of Michael Snow, has so relentlessly and so productively explored the capacity of filmmaking to develop the visual (and auditory) opportunities afforded by the cinematic apparatus itself.” –Scott MacDonald, A CRITICAL CINEMA 5REVERBERATION (1969, 23 min, 16mm)SERENE VELOCITY (1970, 23 min, 16mm, silent)&STILL1971, 54 min, 16mm. Duane Jones (Night of the Living Dead) stars as anthropologist Hess Green, who is stabbed with an ancient ceremonial dagger by his unstable assistant (director Bill Gunn), bestowing upon him the blessing of immortality… and the curse of an unquenchable thirst for blood. When the assistant’s beautiful and outspoken wife Ganja (Marlene Clark) comes searching for her missing husband, she and Hess form an unexpected partnership. Together, they explore just how much power blood holds.

Reuniting stars Jeffrey Combs as Dr. Herbert West and Bruce Abbott as former medical student Dr. Dan Cain, Bride sees the duo expand their experiments to re-animating individual severed limbs. Bride of Re-Animator is an extraordinary follow-up to Brian Yuzna and Screaming Mad George’s previous collaboration Society with an all-star special effects team also includes John Carl Buechler and the KNB EFX Group.

screenings.title: Visible Humans
screenings.description: With artist and ophthalmologist Benjamin Freeman and curator Elisabeth Sherman in person The Visible Human Project began in the late 1990s with sponsorship from the National Library of Medicine. Its aim was to make a complete 3D rendering of the human body for educational use. Now in the public domain, these images raise questions about consent and normative ideals. This evening will interrogate this project and feature a screening of the short film Visible Woman, which is included in our exhibition Overexposed; a presentation by ophthalmologist and photographer Benjamin Freeman; and a discussion including curator Elisabeth Sherman. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission. Special Guests: Elisabeth Sherman is the Robert A. and Elizabeth Rohn Jeffe Chief Curator and Deputy Director at the Museum of the City of New York. Previously, she was Chief Curator and Director of Curatorial Affairs at the International Center of Photography (ICP). Prior to ICP, she was a curator at the Whitney Museum of American Art, where she organized and co-organized many critically acclaimed exhibitions including Dawoud Bey: An American Project, Zoe Leonard: Survey, and Making Knowing: Craft in Art, 1960-2019. At ICP she curated, among others, Naima Green: Instead, I Spin Fantasies, Sheida Soleimani: Panjereh, Yto Barrada: Part Time Abstractionist, and ICP at 50. She is co-editor of the catalog Overexposed: Art, Technology, and the Body. Benji Freeman is a photographer and physician based in New York City. His photography draws from medical epistemologies, techniques, and image archives, investigating the modern aesthetics of caring for others as the actual work of healthcare becomes increasingly automatable. He has taught workshops on photographic technique, the visual culture of medicine, and the anatomy of the visual system, and he has written about the role of photographic perception in medical education. He is currently an ophthalmology resident at Columbia University Medical Center.

screenings.title: The Draughtsman's Contract + Live Performance | Instruments of Desire
screenings.description: Set in a richly exaggerated 17th-century England, Peter Greenaway’s sumptuous and sensuously charged brainteaser catapulted him to the forefront of international art cinema. Adorned with intricate wordplay, extravagant costumes and opulent photography, Greenaway’s first narrative feature weaves a labyrinthine mystery around the maxim “draw what you see, not what you know.” An aristocratic wife (Janet Suzman) commissions a young, cocksure draughtsman (Anthony Higgins) to sketch her husband’s property while he is away—in exchange for a fee, room and board, and one sexual favor for each of the twelve drawings. As the draughtsman becomes more entrenched in the devious schemings in this seemingly idyllic country home, curious details emerge in his drawings that may reveal a murder.

screenings.title: Last Stop for the Circular Ticket
screenings.description: THE THEATER OF THE MATTERS & TAUFIC PRESENT:JEAN-CLAUDE ROUSSEAU’S ‘THE PASTORAL CONCERT’ + ‘LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET’This book launch event celebrates the release of Jean-Claude Rousseau’s unclassifiable, long-unavailable film text, The Pastoral Concert, published for the first time in English this October by Taufic. The evening will culminate in a special premiere screening of Rousseau’s new feature film, LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET (winner of a Jury Special Mention at this year’s FIDMarseille), alongside his 2006 short, FAUX DÉPART.The Pastoral Concert marks the first English translation of Rousseau’s early written work Le Concert champêtre, begun in 1968, some fifteen years before his debut film. Rousseau continued shaping the work as a screenplay until its rejection by the Centre National de la Cinématographie in 1983. Unrealized, Le Concert champêtre became the matrix from which Rousseau’s subsequent films would emerge.Taking its title and three central characters (A, B, and C) from the eponymous painting long attributed to Giorgione and now to Titian, The Pastoral Concert begins as a letter written by a young man to his cousin in the countryside on the eve of her wedding, before mutating into a diary entry, a screenplay, and finally a film imagined through the failure of its own realization. In this restless fluctuation between registers, The Pastoral Concert expresses, in the words of Jean-Marie Straub, “something magnificent [and] entirely different from a screenplay or a découpage.”Translated from the French by artist and filmmaker Kevin Weil, this edition includes an extensive appendix of extra-diegetic materials written by Rousseau, as well as correspondence with contemporaries such as Dominique Noguez, Marcel Hanoun, and Jean-Marie Straub, which form a picture of the work’s early reception.For more info about The Pastoral Concert visit: https://taufic.org/the-pastoral-concertJean-Claude RousseauLAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET / DERNIER ARRÊT POUR LE BILLET CIRCULAIRE2026, 87 min, DCP. No dialogue.Rousseau’s longest film since THE ENCLOSED VALLEY from 1995 (the summit of his 8mm era), LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET refers to the looped ferry route that plies the waters of Lake Como in Northern Italy. Firmly grounded in place, Rousseau’s solitary camera finds desolate poetry in the void of the spectacular landscape and in the anonymous crowds of passengers seemingly entranced at the edge of an abyss. Musical chords and voices magnify their gestures and the movement of the vessel on the lake. Closing the circle, the specter of the end looms: “On the ferry, among the travelers, I recognized Mrs. Death…”Preceded by:Jean-Claude Rousseau FAUX DÉPART (2006, 13 min, DCP. No dialogue.)CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Einsturzende Neubauten: Liebeslieder
screenings.description: An essential text for anyone with a love for the avant-garde. The explosive soundscapes of industrial music titans Einstürzende Neubauten first shook Berlin – then the whole world – to its core in the 1980s. In LIEBESLIEDER, co-directors Klaus Maeck and Johanna Schenkel wield a fractured feast of killer Neubauten performances from Euro television: ones that highlight the group’s cinematic presence, wild handmade instruments, and totally unique style. For those who are at all curious about industrial or noise music in general, this sweaty documentary is unmissable. For Neubauten fans, this humanizing portrait of their first decade provides a fresh take on the band.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!
